full_judgment: 3. The defendant Nos, 1-3 contested the suit by filing a Written Statement denying the plaint's case and totally denying the existence of any oral contract and contending, inter alia, that the story of oral contract is false. There was no contract as alleged in the plaint. The suit is barred by limitation. The plaintiffs have not come up with clean hands. The further case of the defendants are that the defendant No.1 got the suit property from the Government. The Government decided to sell the said suit property to the defendant No.1 at a cost of Tk. 96,843. The defendant No.1 is an employee under the PWD and paid the entire amount from his own pocket in different installments and, as such, the Government executed the sale deed in his favour vide deed No. 6369 dated 15-9-1988. Once, he was suddenly attacked with strong eye disease in both the eyes and was about to become blind. At that stage his sons, the defendant Nos. 2-3, were not grown up enough to understand the official processes. At that time he had to take help of his younger brother i.e. the father of the plaintiff No.2, to assist him to get completed the execution and registration of the sale deed in his favour from the Government. Thereafter, he intended to transfer the suit property in favour of his sons, the defendant Nos. 2-3, and taking the advantage of the defective eyesight of the defendant No.1, the father of the plaintiff No.2 Harunur Rashid (PW 1) started conspiracy to grab the suit property and with that view, he committed theft in the house of the defendants and took away their original documents from his house, beyond his knowledge. The defendant No.1 lodged a GD Entry on 18-6-2000 with Mirpur Police Station. The defendant No.1 got back his eyesight after taking surgical operation and could detect that although he filed application for transfer-permission in favour of his sons, the defendant Nos. 2-3, but that application was replaced by another application for transfer in favour of the plaintiffs. Thereafter, he filed another application on 28-6-2000 for getting permission to transfer of the suit house in favour of his sons, the defendant Nos. 2-3. Thereafter, the Commissioner of Settlement after verification of all those facts found that the defendants Nos. 1-3 are in possession in the suit house with valid title. So, they granted permission dated 10-10-2000 vide Memo No. 728/61/8547/1(4) for transfer of the suit properties in favour of the defendant Nos. 2-3. On the basis of the said permission, the defendant No. I has transferred the suit properties in favour of his sons, the defendant Nos. 2-3, on 18-10-2000 vide Heba deed No. 6206 within the knowledge of the plaintiffs and also within the knowledge of said Harunur Rashid. As a result, the ill intention of Md Harunur Rashid (PW 1) came to an end. The defendants No. 1-3 are enjoying the suit properties by making constructions as per their own arrangements. They are using a portion of the premises as their dwelling house and another portion has been let out to the tenants. Thereafter, said Harunur Rashid, ie. the father of the plaintiff No.2, by using the name of the plaintiffs, had filed the aforementioned suit for Specific Performance of Contract. He also filed a false case against the defendant Nos. 1-3 on 23-12-2000 with the Mirpur Police Station being Mirpur PS Case No. 83(12)2000 under sections 143/448/ 323/379/506 of the Penal Code and on the plea of the aforesaid case, the PW 1 with the help of local police, started conspiracy against the defendants so that they are compelled to hide themselves until bail is granted. Thereafter, Harunur Rashid trespassed into the suit premises on 23-12-2000 during the pendency of the said criminal case. Thereafter, the matter was brought to the notice of the learned Assistant Judge. The defendant Nos. 1-3 also filed a petition for restoration of possession before the learned Assistant Judge on 24-6-2001 and that application was kept with the record for disposal. The defendants No.1-3 also filed a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession against the said Harunur Rashid (PW 1) and his men before the learned Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 118 of 2002 which on transfer is still pending before the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka as being Title Suit No. 116 of 2003.
